skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through disciplined root-cause investigation before implementing fixes for bugs, test failures, build errors, and unexpected behavior.
skill.summary: Apply a structured root-cause workflow before changing code.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: I reviewed the static findings in context. The Ruby backtick, reconnaissance, environment-file, and device-file hits are false positives from Markdown fences, TypeScript template literals, safe NODE_ENV checks, and a manual test helper. One medium semantic issue remains because a debugging example can encourage logging environment and keychain state without redaction.

remediation.issue: Diagnostic example can leak environment or signing metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Change the example to log only SET or UNSET states, remove broad env output, and warn users to redact CI logs.

remediation.issue: Helper script executes project tests for every matched file.
remediation.suggestion: Mark find-polluter.sh as manual-only, require users to inspect the pattern, and document that it runs repository test code.

remediation.issue: Executable helpers and documentation examples are mixed in the same skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as non-install hooks and keep helper scripts documented with expected inputs and effects.

semantic_findings.description: The debugging example tells users to inspect environment variables matching IDENTITY and keychain identity state. If copied into CI logs without redaction, this can expose signing or deployment metadata.

content.value_statement: Random fixes can waste time and create new defects. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through evidence-based debugging before fixes.
actual_capabilities: Enforces a four-phase workflow: investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis testing, and implementation.
Prompts users to reproduce failures, read errors, check recent changes, and gather evidence.
Provides root-cause tracing guidance for bugs that surface deep in a call stack.
Includes condition-based waiting patterns for flaky asynchronous tests.
Shows defense-in-depth validation patterns after the root cause is understood.
Includes a helper script for finding tests that create unwanted files or state.
limitations: Does not diagnose a bug without project logs, test output, or reproducible steps.
May add time upfront when a safe emergency mitigation is required first.
Documentation examples must be adapted to the user's language, framework, and security policy.
The helper script assumes an npm test workflow and may need changes for other runners.

use_cases.title: Investigate Test Failures
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to reproduce a failing test, inspect errors, and form one evidence-backed hypothesis before editing code.

use_cases.title: Reduce Flaky Async Tests
use_cases.description: Replace guess-based sleeps with condition-based waiting after identifying the actual state or event the test needs.

use_cases.title: Review Incident Fixes
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed production fix addresses the root cause or only hides the visible symptom.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Bug Investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single failure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic debugging on this failure. Read the error, list the evidence we have, and tell me the next investigation step before any fix: [failure details].

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Bad Value
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for bugs deep in a call stack.
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace this bad value backward through the call chain. Identify the immediate cause, each caller, and the original trigger before recommending a fix: [trace or logs].

prompt_templates.title: Replace Flaky Waiting
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for asynchronous test failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this flaky test. Find the condition it should wait for, explain why current timing is unreliable, and propose a condition-based waiting plan: [test behavior].

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Failed Fix Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt after several unsuccessful fixes.
prompt_templates.prompt: We have tried multiple fixes and each failed. Apply the systematic debugging process, identify untested assumptions, and decide whether the architecture should be questioned: [attempt history].

output_examples.input: A payment test intermittently stays pending after several sleep increases.
output_examples.output: The skill would stop further sleep changes, inspect status update flow, reproduce the failure, and define the real completion condition.

output_examples.input: A test run creates repository state in the wrong directory.
output_examples.output: The skill would trace the directory value from the failing operation back through each caller until the first invalid value is found.

output_examples.input: A proposed fix passed once but failed on the next run.
output_examples.output: The skill would reject adding more changes on top, record the failed hypothesis, and return to evidence gathering.

best_practices: Collect logs, errors, recent changes, and reproduction steps before editing code.
Change one variable at a time so each hypothesis has a clear result.
After finding the root cause, add tests and validation at relevant layers.
anti_patterns: Applying a familiar fix before proving it matches the current failure.
Increasing timeouts to hide flaky behavior without identifying the awaited condition.
Bundling refactors with the bug fix before the hypothesis is verified.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for bugs, failing tests, build errors, performance issues, and unexpected behavior before proposing fixes.

faq.question: Does this skill write code for me?
faq.answer: It guides the debugging process. Code changes should come after the root cause and hypothesis are clear.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes condition-based waiting guidance for replacing arbitrary sleeps with reliable state checks.

faq.question: Is it useful during production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes, but urgent mitigation may come first when safety requires it. The root-cause process should still follow.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the exact error, logs, reproduction steps, recent changes, and any fixes already attempted.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
